correction.text: the Laigin's lands in the east: Dublin, Kildare, Wicklow, Wexford, Carlow and Laois; Meath lost to the Southern Ui Neill and Osraige to Munster

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Leinster. The page names no counties for the early kingdom; the list is the researcher's reading of 'the east of the island' with the two losses it names ('The Southern Ui Neill took the Kingdom of Meath, and Osraige went to the Corcu Loigde, becoming part of the Kingdom of Munster'). Infobox: 'Established: 7th century BC' (traditional, Ugaine Mor 634-594 BC); no area given.

correction.text: Leinster without the Norse enclave at Dublin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'the Vikings had set up their Kingdom of Dublin from territory previously belonging to Leinster' (Leinster article); the Dublin article dates the Kingdom of Dublin 'Established: 853'. The 25 km circle is the researcher's reading.

correction.text: Leinster with Osraige regained ('In the 9th century, the Laighin also regained control of Osraige') and without the Norse enclave at Dublin

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the Osraige gain is undated beyond the 9th century, so 900 is a rounding. Wexford was also a Viking port ('Ui Imair Vikings established themselves at Dublin and Wexford') but is kept inside as Diarmait's own seat.

correction.text: the MacMurrough-Kavanagh kingdom: 'much of what is today County Wexford and County Carlow' and parts of Wicklow until the early 17th century

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the Norman grant of 1171 the page gives no territory until 'Art MacMurrough-Kavanagh ... ruled from 1375 to 1417'; the Gaelic revival began 'after 1350' (Lordship article). Counties named by the lead; extent within them is soft.

region.text: the Laigin's kingdom in the east of the island

ledger.note: The kingdom of the Laigin: traditional founding 'Established: 7th century BC' (infobox, Ugaine Mor 634-594 BC), a legendary date. The 5th to early 8th century kingship was contested by Ui Cheinnselaig, Ui Bairrche and Ui Mail; 400 is the researcher's opening of the historical record, confidence 1.

region.text: Dublin, where the Ui Imair Vikings 'established themselves at Dublin and Wexford' from the 9th century

ledger.note: 853: the Norse Kingdom of Dublin appears. Dublin article: infobox 'Established: 853'; Leinster article: 'the Vikings had set up their Kingdom of Dublin from territory previously belonging to Leinster'; Murchad mac Diarmata 'took control of the Kingdom of Dublin for a brief period' (undated).

region.text: Osraige (Kilkenny), regained by the Laighin in the 9th century

ledger.note: 9th century: Leinster regains Osraige. 'In the 9th century, the Laighin also regained control of Osraige.' No year is given; 900 is the researcher's rounding.

region.text: Leinster, granted to Strongbow: 'Richard FitzGilbert, count of Strigoil, became lord of Leinster'

ledger.note: 1171: Diarmait dies (about 1 May) and the Normans take Leinster. 'died a few months later (about 1 May 1171)'; 'Richard FitzGilbert ... became lord of Leinster'; Diarmait's son 'Donnchad became the king of Leinster after his father's death in 1171' (Leinster article). Henry II's grant of Leinster to Strongbow as a fiefdom is dated 1171 in the Lordship article.

region.text: the MacMurrough-Kavanagh lands in Wexford, Carlow and Wicklow

ledger.note: 1375: Art MacMurrough-Kavanagh begins his reign (to 1417). The page gives his reign, not a conquest; the return of this land to Gaelic kings is bridged from the Gaelic revival 'after 1350'.

region.text: the last Leinster lands: 'it became part of the Tudor Kingdom of Ireland'

ledger.note: 1603: the kingdom ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 1603'; the lead says it persisted 'until the early 17th century' and was absorbed into the Tudor Kingdom of Ireland.

wars.name: Norman invasion of Ireland (Leinster phase)
wars.outcome: Ruaidri deposed Mac Murchada (1166 or 1167, the page conflicts); Normans landed at Bannow Bay, Wexford fell May 1169, Waterford and Dublin in 1170; Mac Murchada died about 1 May 1171 and Strongbow became lord of Leinster.

certainty.note: No page gives a boundary; the kingdom is the east of the island with named losses and gains.

notes: Founding is traditional (infobox 7th century BC); the dossier starts at 400 for the historical record and the reviewer may prefer the infobox year. Gaelic Leinster 1171-1375 has no territory because the pages give none; the Lordship dossier's Leinster keyframes (1171-1347) cover the same land. The Kavanagh keyframe 1375-1603 sits inside land the Lordship dossier says it lost in 1348 to Gaelic lordships. The Leinster dynasties (Ui Dunlainge, Ui Cheinnselaig) are named on the page without reign years, so no ruler strip. Counterparts: kingdom-of-munster, kingdom-of-dublin and kingdom-of-meath (the Southern Ui Neill) all have dossiers in this batch.
